newsitem.title: USA: SOCCER-MLS' FLOUNDERING GALAXY FIRE COACH OSIANDER.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MLS' FLOUNDERING GALAXY FIRE COACH OSIANDER.

text.p: The Los Angeles Galaxy, mired at the bottom of the Major League Soccer standings after reaching the championship game last season, fired head coach Lothar Osiander on Tuesday.

"We felt we had to try something different," said club President and General Manager Danny Villanueva. "We have more than half a season remaining and we plan on being a force in the playoffs," he told reporters at the Rose Bowl in Pasadena.

A replacement for the German-born Osiander, whose team has only seven points and a won-lost record of 3-9 this season, was not named. The move came after Sunday's disappointing 1-0 loss to the New England Revolution - the Galaxy's fourth in five shootouts this season.
Osiander's assistant coach, Ecuadoran-born Octavio Zambrano was named interim head coach and is among several candidates for the top job, the club said.

In the inaugural MLS season last year, the Galaxy, boasting flamboyant Mexican goalkeeper Jorge Campos and U.S. World Cup star Cobi Jones, won its first 12 games on the way to capturing the Western Division championship.
The team played Washington D.C. United in the league championship game, but lost 3-2 in overtime, after leading the match 2-0 with less than 20 minutes to play.
